subject: Civil Engineering
title: Rigid Frames: When Joints Don't Rotate
description: Learn Rigid Frames: When Joints Don't Rotate in one minute.

hook.text: A doorframe stays square even when you push on it. The corners are rigid.

buildup.text: Rigid frames have welded or reinforced joints that resist rotation, unlike pin joints.

discovery.text: This stiffness lets the frame resist lateral loads — wind, earthquakes, impact.

twist.text: Most modern buildings are rigid frames — steel or concrete moment-resisting joints.

climax.text: Without rigid frames, skyscrapers would sway too far and crack their walls.

punchline.text: Lock the joints and the whole frame stands stiff.

quiz.question: What makes a rigid frame different from a truss?
options: Rigid frames use cables instead of bars
Rigid frames have joints that resist rotation, not just pin connections
Rigid frames can only be made of wood

details.summary: Rigid frames use moment-resistant connections between beams and columns that prevent relative rotation at the joints. This transfers bending moments from beams into columns, reducing beam moments and enabling frames to resist lateral forces from wind and earthquake without diagonal bracing.
details.whyItMatters: Rigid frames are the primary structural system for multi-story buildings worldwide. They resist gravity and lateral loads while providing the open floor plans that modern architecture demands.
takeaways: Moment connections transfer bending between beams and columns at the joints
Rigid frames resist lateral wind and earthquake forces without diagonal bracing
Column bending moments increase significantly compared to pin-connected frames

faq.question: How do rigid frames resist lateral forces without bracing?
faq.answer: When wind pushes on a rigid frame, the moment connections force beams and columns to bend together in a coordinated pattern. Beams resist the lateral force through their bending stiffness transmitted to columns through the rigid joints.

faq.question: Why are the connections in rigid frames so critical?
faq.answer: Moment connections must transfer large bending moments and shear forces between beam flanges and column flanges. Connection failure converts the rigid frame to a mechanism that collapses sideways.
